sections.content: Institutional history leans on passive voice constantly: a viceroyalty was created, a territory was administered, a system was designed — the institution is the subject, not necessarily the specific person behind it. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El virreinato de Nueva España fue creado en 1535; el virreinato del Perú fue establecido en 1542.
items.english: The Viceroyalty of New Spain was created in 1535; the Viceroyalty of Peru was established in 1542.

items.spanish: Fueron creados dos virreinatos adicionales, el de Nueva Granada y el del Río de la Plata.
items.english: Two additional viceroyalties were created, New Granada and Río de la Plata.

items.spanish: Todo el comercio con las colonias estaba controlado por una sola institución, la Casa de Contratación.
items.english: All trade with the colonies was controlled by a single institution, the Casa de Contratación.

items.spanish: Este sistema fue diseñado para mantener el control sobre un territorio enorme.
items.english: This system was designed to maintain control over an enormous territory.

sections.content: Ser + participle + estar + participle both describe a passive state, but they answer slightly different questions: fue creado marks the moment of an action (creation happened then), while estaba controlado describes an ongoing condition (control existed over a stretch of time). Institutional history uses both constantly, often in the same paragraph.
